newsitem.title: HUNGARY: New group says it exploded Budapest bombs.
newsitem.headline: New group says it exploded Budapest bombs.

text.p: A organisation calling itself the Hungarian Will of Gods (IMA) has claimed responsibility for two bomb blasts in Budapest near Europe's largest synanogue.

The Hungarian daily Mai Nap said a telephone caller on Thursday said the previously-unknown organisation planted the bomb which exploded in a dustbin near the Dohany utca synagogue on Wednesday night.

The man said it also planted a bomb which blew up on August 25 on a bench in Klauzal Square, about 100 metres (yards) from a kosher restaurant in the heart of the former Jewish ghetto in the Hungarian capital.
The bombs did not hurt anyone but heightened concerns in Hungary's Jewish community.

Police spokesman Laszlo Garamvolgyi told Reuters that they were searching intensively for the bombers as well as the man who telephoned to Mai Nap. "It is not sure yet that (the caller) was the culprit," he said.
